value_source: DSS Data Exchange, Commonwealth Home Support Programme protocols
variable_description: What the assistance recorded on this row cost to deliver. It is the provider's own reported cost rather than a price or a subsidy, so it measures what was spent on the service and not what the recipient paid or what government contributed. Read with ASSISTANCE_MINUTES_NBR and ASSISTANCE_QUANTITY_NBR it gives a cost per hour or per unit, which is the only way to compare service intensity across providers whose units differ.
value_definition: A dollar amount for the assistance on this row. Reporting requirements changed over the life of the programme, so an amount is only comparable within a reporting period.
limitation: Cost reporting is not audited and providers apply overheads differently, so a difference between providers can be an accounting difference rather than a real one. A zero or missing amount often means the cost was not reported rather than that the service was free.
rationale: The Commonwealth Home Support Programme protocols define the assistance attributes reported against a service delivery record in the Data Exchange, which is the collection this clearinghouse field is drawn from.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the one-line curated description 'Cost amount of assistance provided.' with no value domain, so the page repeated the generic no-value-list sentence twice.

value_source: DSS Data Exchange, Commonwealth Home Support Programme protocols
variable_description: How long the assistance on this row took, in minutes. Minutes are the comparable unit across service types where quantity is not: an hour of domestic assistance and an hour of nursing are both sixty minutes, while their quantity counts mean different things. Not every service type reports minutes, so this column is populated for time-based services and empty for others.
value_definition: A count of minutes, not hours. Services delivered in a group setting report the recipient's own minutes rather than the session's length.
limitation: An empty value means minutes were not the reporting unit for that service type, not that no time was spent, so treating blanks as zero understates delivery. Minutes measure contact, not benefit, and a service delivered efficiently records fewer of them.
rationale: The Commonwealth Home Support Programme protocols define the assistance attributes reported against a service delivery record in the Data Exchange.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the one-line curated description 'Number of minutes of assistance provided.' with no value domain.

value_source: DSS Data Exchange, Commonwealth Home Support Programme protocols
variable_description: How much assistance was delivered, counted in whatever unit that service type uses. The unit is not carried on this column, so a quantity is meaningless without the service type beside it: meals, trips, hours and visits all appear here as bare numbers. Comparing quantities across service types adds meals to trips.
value_definition: A count in the service type's own unit. The unit is fixed by the service type rather than recorded per row.
limitation: The column cannot be summed across service types, which is the mistake it invites, and it cannot be compared with ASSISTANCE_MINUTES_NBR because the two measure different things for the same service. A quantity of one can be a single meal or a full day of respite.
rationale: The Commonwealth Home Support Programme protocols define the assistance attributes reported against a service delivery record in the Data Exchange, with the unit of measure set by the service type.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the one-line curated description 'Quantity of assistance provided.' with no value domain, and nothing warned that the unit varies by service type.

value_source: ABS, Australian Statistical Geography Standard, Statistical Area Level 2
variable_description: Where the aged care service outlet is, as a 2016 SA2. It is the outlet's location and not the recipient's, so it answers where care is delivered from rather than where the people receiving it live, and the two diverge most for home-based services and for rural recipients travelling to a regional centre. The 2016 vintage matters: SA2 boundaries changed in the 2021 ASGS, so this cannot be joined to a 2021 SA2 without a correspondence.
value_definition: A nine-digit ASGS 2016 SA2 code whose leading digit is the state. SA2s are designed to represent communities that interact socially and economically, with populations generally between 3,000 and 25,000.
limitation: An outlet's SA2 is a service supply measure, not a demand one, and reading it as a recipient location overstates services in regional centres and understates them in the surrounding areas. A provider that reports one head-office outlet for services delivered across a wide area concentrates all of it in one SA2.
rationale: The field is an SA2 code at the 2016 ASGS vintage on the aged care outlet table. The ABS publishes the SA2 definition and design criteria.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried a one-line curated description with no value domain, and nothing said that the code is the outlet's rather than the recipient's or that the vintage blocks a 2021 join.

value_source: DSS Data Exchange, Commonwealth Home Support Programme protocols
variable_description: Whether the care recipient identifies as having a disability, impairment or long-term condition. It is the summary flag that the five group-specific indicators sit under, so it should be set whenever any of them is, and a recipient flagged here with no group set is one whose disability was recorded without being classified. In an aged care collection the flag is harder to read than it looks, because age-related frailty and disability are recorded differently by different assessors.
value_definition: An indicator, not a severity or a diagnosis. The group indicators beside it split it into intellectual or learning, physical or diverse, psychiatric, sensory or speech, and unspecified.
limitation: The flag records self-identification at assessment, so it measures disclosure as much as disability, and an older person who does not think of their impairment as a disability is not counted. It says nothing about severity or about whether the disability is what brought the person to aged care.
rationale: The Commonwealth Home Support Programme protocols define the disability attributes recorded against a care recipient in the Data Exchange.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried a one-line curated description with no value domain, and nothing explained its relationship to the five group indicators.

value_source: DSS Data Exchange, Commonwealth Home Support Programme protocols
variable_description: Whether the care recipient has an intellectual or learning disability. It is one of five group indicators that sit under DISABILITY_IND, and the groups are not exclusive: a recipient can be flagged in several, so the five do not sum to the summary flag. This group matters in aged care because people with lifelong intellectual disability age earlier and enter the system younger than the general population.
value_definition: An indicator for the disability group, not a severity or a diagnosis.
limitation: The groups overlap, so counting flags counts conditions rather than people. Dementia and other acquired cognitive impairment are not this group, and assessors do not always separate the two, which inflates it in an older cohort.
rationale: The Commonwealth Home Support Programme protocols define the disability group indicators recorded against a care recipient in the Data Exchange.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried a one-line curated description with no value domain, and nothing said the groups overlap.

value_source: DSS Data Exchange, Commonwealth Home Support Programme protocols
variable_description: Whether the care recipient has a physical or diverse disability. It is the most common of the five group indicators in an aged care collection, because mobility limitation is what brings most people to home support in the first place. That commonness is also what makes it least discriminating: a flag here separates a recipient from almost nobody else in the file.
value_definition: An indicator for the disability group, not a severity or a diagnosis. 'Diverse' covers conditions such as chronic illness that are not neatly physical, sensory or psychiatric.
limitation: The groups overlap, so counting flags counts conditions rather than people. The flag does not distinguish a lifelong physical disability from age-related decline, which are different pathways into aged care with different service needs.
rationale: The Commonwealth Home Support Programme protocols define the disability group indicators recorded against a care recipient in the Data Exchange.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried a one-line curated description with no value domain.

value_source: DSS Data Exchange, Commonwealth Home Support Programme protocols
variable_description: Whether the care recipient has a psychiatric disability. Of the five group indicators this is the one most affected by disclosure: mental health is under-reported at aged care assessment relative to its prevalence, so a flag here is strong evidence and its absence is weak evidence. It is also the group most likely to appear alongside another, because psychiatric disability and physical limitation commonly co-occur in an older cohort.
value_definition: An indicator for the disability group, not a severity or a diagnosis.
limitation: The groups overlap, so counting flags counts conditions rather than people. Under-reporting means the flag cannot be used to estimate mental health prevalence among aged care recipients, only to identify people for whom it was recorded.
rationale: The Commonwealth Home Support Programme protocols define the disability group indicators recorded against a care recipient in the Data Exchange.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried a one-line curated description with no value domain.

value_source: DSS Data Exchange, Commonwealth Home Support Programme protocols
variable_description: Whether the care recipient has a sensory or speech disability. It groups vision, hearing and speech together, which in an older cohort mostly means age-related hearing and vision loss rather than lifelong sensory disability. The distinction matters for service design, because a hearing-impaired recipient needs a different kind of contact from a vision-impaired one and this column does not separate them.
value_definition: An indicator for the disability group, not a severity or a diagnosis. Vision, hearing and speech share the one flag.
limitation: The groups overlap, so counting flags counts conditions rather than people. Because vision, hearing and speech are not separated, the column cannot support any analysis that turns on which sense is affected.
rationale: The Commonwealth Home Support Programme protocols define the disability group indicators recorded against a care recipient in the Data Exchange.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried a one-line curated description with no value domain.

value_source: DSS Data Exchange, Commonwealth Home Support Programme protocols
variable_description: Whether a disability was recorded for the care recipient without being placed in one of the four named groups. It is the residual of the five group indicators, so it is best read as a data quality signal rather than a category: a high rate across a provider's records means their assessors are not classifying, not that their recipients have unusual conditions.
value_definition: An indicator for the residual disability group, not a severity or a diagnosis.
limitation: The flag describes the recording rather than the person, so including it in a disability profile mixes a measurement artefact with a condition. A recipient flagged here may in fact belong to one of the four named groups.
rationale: The Commonwealth Home Support Programme protocols define the disability group indicators recorded against a care recipient in the Data Exchange, with a residual for disabilities recorded without a group.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried a one-line curated description with no value domain, and nothing said the column is a data quality signal.
